newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: European MPs say Hague court could rule on Kashmir.
newsitem.headline: European MPs say Hague court could rule on Kashmir.

text.p: European parliamentarians proposed on Tuesday that India and Pakistan submit their dispute over Kashmir to the International Court of Justice in The Hague.

"As a delegation we suggested that the Kashmir issue be sent to the International Court of Justice in The Hague because the court has been set up by the United Nations to resolve territorial disputes between states," Jan Weibenga, a Dutch member of the European Parliament, told a news conference.
Weibenga, one of four members of the European Parliament who arrived in Pakistan on Saturday, said the idea had been proposed to Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif earlier on Tuesday.
"His (Sharif's) response was neither positive nor negative but his present policy is to open up dialogue with India," he said.

Anita Pollack from Britain said Sharif had told the delegation he would discuss the suggestion with Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral during informal talks at a regional summit in the Maldives capital Male from May 12 to 14.
India and Pakistan have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over Kashmir.
India says Kashmir is an integral part of its territory and wants only bilateral talks with Pakistan.

Pakistan has said it would welcome outside help to resolve the dispute. It wants mainly Moslem Kashmiris to be allowed to vote in an internationally supervised plebiscite whether to join Islamic Pakistan or Hindu-majority India.
Weibenga said that if bilateral talks failed, either India or Pakistan could approach the International Court of Justice.
"There may be other ways of resolving the conflict, other than of course the military way," he said.

"At the moment the concern of the international community is that no fourth war should be fought on the Kashmir issue, and this is also because of the nuclear element, so it is also our interest that a peaceful solution is found to the problem."
Pakistan and India deny having nuclear weapons, but Western officials say both could assemble them quickly.
